protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_id: UniProt accession number — primary key for all Swiss-Prot reviewed protein records (e.g. 'P04637' for TP53, 'P00533' for EGFR, 'P31946' for YWHAB). Always the canonical form without isoform suffix. Users may ask for 'UniProt ID', 'UniProt accession', 'UniProt entry', or 'protein accession'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.entry_name: UniProt mnemonic entry name in the format <GENE>_<SPECIES> (e.g. 'P53_HUMAN', 'EGFR_HUMAN', '1433B_HUMAN'). Unique identifier within UniProt; users may ask for 'UniProt entry name', 'mnemonic', or 'UniProt name'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_name: Full recommended protein name from UniProt (e.g. 'Cellular tumor antigen p53', 'Epidermal growth factor receptor', '14-3-3 protein beta/alpha'). Users may ask for 'protein name', 'protein description', or 'full protein name'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.gene_symbol: HGNC official gene symbol for this protein (e.g. 'TP53', 'EGFR', 'YWHAB', 'BRCA1'). Users may ask for 'gene', 'gene symbol', 'HGNC symbol', or 'gene name'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.ensembl_accession: Ensembl gene identifier, normalised to the bare ENSG form (version and isoform suffix stripped by the loader, e.g. 'ENSG00000141510'). Internal cross-reference; users may ask for 'Ensembl ID' or 'ENSG ID'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.entrez: NCBI Entrez gene ID as a bare integer string (e.g. '7157' for TP53, '1956' for EGFR). Internal cross-reference; users may ask for 'Entrez ID', 'NCBI gene ID', or 'Entrez gene'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.organism: Full organism name including common name in parentheses (e.g. 'Homo sapiens (Human)'). All 20,431 rows in this table are human. Users may ask for 'organism', 'species', or 'taxon'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.reviewed: Whether the entry is Swiss-Prot manually reviewed (always 'true' for this table). Users may ask for 'reviewed', 'Swiss-Prot', or 'curated'.
protein_master_table_uniprot.hgnc: HGNC identifier with 'HGNC:' prefix (e.g. 'HGNC:11998' for TP53, 'HGNC:3236' for EGFR). Internal cross-reference; users may ask for 'HGNC ID'.

gene_protein_association_uniprot.protein_id: UniProt accession — FK to protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_id. Maps a gene symbol to its canonical UniProt protein.
gene_protein_association_uniprot.ensembl_accession: Ensembl gene ID, normalised to the bare ENSG form (e.g. 'ENSG00000141510'). Cross-reference for Ensembl-based lookups.
gene_protein_association_uniprot.entrez: NCBI Entrez gene ID as a bare integer string. Cross-reference for Entrez-based lookups.

keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_id: UniProt keyword controlled vocabulary ID (e.g. 'KW-0001', 'KW-0002'). Primary key; internal identifier.
keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_name: UniProt keyword human-readable name (e.g. '3D-structure', 'Actin-binding', 'Alternative splicing', 'Zinc-finger'). Users may ask for 'keyword', 'UniProt keyword', or 'functional keyword'.
keyword_master_uniprot.category: Broad category grouping the keyword (e.g. 'Ligand', 'Biological process', 'Technical term', 'Molecular function', 'Disease', 'PTM', 'Cellular component'). Users may ask for 'keyword category', 'keyword type', or 'functional category'.
keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_description: Full text definition of the keyword concept. Long-form description used for semantic search.
keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_synonyms: Semicolon-separated list ('; ') of alternative names for the keyword, terminated by a period. Used to match user queries that use non-canonical vocabulary.
keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_entry_type: Type of keyword entry — 'ID' for most entries, 'IC' for category-header entries. Internal metadata field.
keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_hierarchy: Hierarchical path of the keyword within the UniProt keyword taxonomy (e.g. 'Biological process > Cell cycle'). Used to understand keyword parent-child relationships.

subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_id: UniProt subcellular location controlled vocabulary ID (e.g. 'SL-0476', 'SL-0002'). Primary key; internal identifier.
subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_name: Human-readable subcellular location name (e.g. 'Nucleus', 'Cytoplasm', 'Cell membrane', 'Mitochondrion', 'Endoplasmic reticulum', 'A band'). Users may ask for 'subcellular location', 'cellular compartment', or 'organelle'.
subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_description: Full text definition of the subcellular location concept. Long-form description.
subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_synonyms: Semicolon-separated ('; ') alternative names for the location, terminated by a period (e.g. 'TJ; Zonula occludens.'). Often null. Used to match user queries with non-standard vocabulary.
subcell_location_uniprot.keyword_id: Associated UniProt keyword ID (KW-NNNN) for this location — FK to keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_id.
subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_hierarchy: Hierarchical path within the UniProt subcellular location taxonomy (e.g. 'Cell > Cytoplasm > Organelle > Mitochondrion').
subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_entry_type: Type of location entry — 'ID' (location), 'IO' (orientation), or 'IT' (topology). Internal metadata field.

gene_ontology_uniprot.protein_id: UniProt accession — FK to protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_id. Used to join GO annotations to a specific protein.
gene_ontology_uniprot.qualifier: GO relationship qualifier describing how the gene product relates to the GO term. 22 distinct values: the four most common positives are 'enables' (molecular function role), 'involved_in' (biological process participation), 'located_in' (subcellular location), 'part_of' (component membership); plus 'is_active_in', 'acts_upstream_of', 'acts_upstream_of_or_within', 'contributes_to', 'colocalizes_with' (and *_positive_effect/*_negative_effect variants), each also occurring with a 'NOT|' negation prefix (e.g. 'NOT|enables'). Users may ask for 'qualifier', 'GO relation', or 'association type'.
gene_ontology_uniprot.go_id: Gene Ontology term identifier (e.g. 'GO:0005515' for protein binding, 'GO:0006915' for apoptotic process). Used as a filter when the user provides a specific GO ID. Users may ask for 'GO ID', 'GO term ID', or 'ontology term'.
gene_ontology_uniprot.db_reference: Source database reference supporting this annotation (e.g. 'PMID:33961781', 'GO_REF:0000033'). Internal provenance field.
gene_ontology_uniprot.evidence: GO evidence code categorising how the annotation was established (22 distinct codes). Top values by frequency: IEA (Inferred from Electronic Annotation, ~135K), IDA (Inferred from Direct Assay, ~78K), IBA (Inferred from Biological Aspect of Ancestor, ~60K), TAS (Traceable Author Statement, ~34K), ISS (Inferred from Sequence or Structural Similarity, ~32K), IMP (Inferred from Mutant Phenotype, ~23K), IPI (Inferred from Physical Interaction, ~22K), NAS (Non-traceable Author Statement, ~17K), EXP (Inferred from Experiment, ~9K), HDA (High-throughput Direct Assay, ~7K); long tail includes IGI, ISA, IC, HTP, IEP, ND, RCA, HMP, HEP, IKR, ISO, ISM. Users may ask for 'evidence code', 'evidence type', or 'annotation quality'.
gene_ontology_uniprot.aspect: GO ontology namespace. Enum: {'F' (Molecular Function — what the protein does biochemically), 'P' (Biological Process — the larger cellular or physiological role), 'C' (Cellular Component — where the protein resides)}. Users may ask for 'GO aspect', 'GO namespace', 'molecular function', 'biological process', or 'cellular component'.

variant_disease_uniprot.protein_id: UniProt accession — FK to protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_id. Identifies the protein in which this variant occurs.
variant_disease_uniprot.ftid: UniProt feature identifier for the variant (e.g. 'VAR_018369', 'VAR_005932' for TP53 p.Arg175His). Internal variant identifier in UniProt feature annotations; not row-unique — one ftid can recur across multiple disease rows.
variant_disease_uniprot.swiss_prot_change: HGVS protein-level amino acid change notation (e.g. 'p.His52Arg', 'p.Arg175His', 'p.Gly12Val'). Users may ask for 'protein change', 'amino acid substitution', 'variant notation', or 'HGVS notation'.
variant_disease_uniprot.variant_type: Clinical significance classification. Enum: {'US' (Uncertain Significance), 'LP/P' (Likely Pathogenic / Pathogenic), 'LB/B' (Likely Benign / Benign)}. Users may ask for 'pathogenicity', 'clinical significance', 'variant classification', or 'variant type'.
variant_disease_uniprot.dbsnp: dbSNP reference SNP identifier with 'rs' prefix (e.g. 'rs893184', 'rs28934578'). Cross-reference to dbSNP; may be null for novel variants. Users may ask for 'rsID', 'rs number', 'SNP ID', or 'dbSNP'.
variant_disease_uniprot.disease_id: Internal disease ontology identifier for associated disease — ALWAYS NULL in this snapshot (100%, 84,476/84,476 rows). Use omim_id or disease_name for disease-based filtering instead. Internal cross-reference field.
variant_disease_uniprot.disease_name: Full disease name associated with this variant, often including MIM number (e.g. 'Achalasia-addisonianism-alacrima syndrome (AAAS) [MIM:231550]', 'Li-Fraumeni syndrome [MIM:151623]'). Users may ask for 'disease', 'associated disease', 'disease name', or 'clinical phenotype'.
variant_disease_uniprot.omim_id: OMIM disease identifier for the associated disease, as a bare integer string with no 'OMIM:' prefix (e.g. '231550' for Achalasia-addisonianism-alacrima syndrome, '151623' for Li-Fraumeni syndrome). Extracted from the inline '[MIM:NNNNNN]' tag of disease_name; null for 54.0% of rows (45,589/84,476). Users may ask for 'OMIM ID' or 'MIM number'.

id_mapping_uniprot.protein_id: UniProt accession — FK to protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_id. Maps one protein to potentially many external identifiers.
id_mapping_uniprot.db: Target database name for this ID mapping. Enum of all 10 observed values: 'Ensembl', 'Ensembl_PRO', 'Ensembl_TRS', 'GeneID', 'Gene_Name', 'Gene_Synonym', 'HGNC', 'RefSeq', 'RefSeq_NT', 'UniProtKB-ID'. (No PDB cross-references in this snapshot.) Used to filter the external ID by database type.
id_mapping_uniprot.external_id: The identifier in the target database (e.g. 'P53_HUMAN' for UniProtKB-ID, 'ENSG00000141510.20' for Ensembl — versioned here, unlike the bare ENSG form in protein_master_table — '7157' for GeneID, 'HGNC:11998' for HGNC). Users may ask for 'external ID', 'cross-reference', or 'mapped ID'.

protein_keyword_uniprot.keyword_id: UniProt keyword controlled-vocabulary ID (KW-NNNN) — FK to keyword_master_uniprot.keyword_id; join there for keyword_name / category

protein_subcell_uniprot.subcell_id: UniProt subcellular-location controlled-vocabulary ID (SL-NNNN) — FK to subcell_location_uniprot.subcell_id; join there for subcell_name

protein_function_uniprot.function_text: Full free-text FUNCTION annotation from Swiss-Prot CC -!- FUNCTION lines (ECO evidence tags stripped). Describes the protein's biochemical activity, biological role, pathway involvement, and known interactors. Examples: "Catalytic subunit of the cyclin-dependent kinase 9...", "Serine/threonine kinase that acts as a tumor suppressor...". Match user queries about protein function, role, activity, or mechanism using this field.

ptm_sites_uniprot.position: Sequence position of the modified residue as an integer string (e.g. "133", "308", "5"). Do NOT include amino-acid prefix — NOT "Ser-133", just "133". Rare isoform-specific coordinates use "accession-isoform:position" format (e.g. "P31946-2:1"). Users may ask for "phosphorylated residue", "modified site", or "modification position".
ptm_sites_uniprot.modification: Type of post-translational modification at this site (e.g. "Phosphoserine", "Phosphothreonine", "N6-acetyllysine", "N6-methyllysine", "Asymmetric dimethylarginine"). Users may ask for "PTM type", "modification type", "phosphorylation", "acetylation", "methylation", "ubiquitination". Values come from UniProt controlled vocabulary.
ptm_sites_uniprot.enzymes: Curated enzyme(s) that catalyse this PTM (e.g. "PKA", "CK1", "PLK1", "Aurora-A"), extracted from the /note=by <enzyme> annotation. Null when the modifying enzyme is not curated. Users may ask "which kinase phosphorylates protein X?" or "what enzyme modifies position Y?".

protein_interaction_uniprot.protein_id: UniProt accession of the bait/anchor protein — FK to protein_master_table_uniprot.protein_id
protein_interaction_uniprot.interaction_type: Type of interaction record: "SUBUNIT" = free-text subunit/complex description from CC -!- SUBUNIT (includes homodimer/heterodimer/complex/binding statements); "BINARY" = structured binary PPI from CC -!- INTERACTION with IntAct experiment counts. For text-based partner searches, use SUBUNIT rows with description. For counting distinct partners, prefer BINARY rows.
protein_interaction_uniprot.interactor_gene: Gene symbol of the interacting partner (BINARY rows only; null for SUBUNIT rows). Examples: "TP53", "MDM2", "BRCA1". Use to look up "what does protein X interact with?" or "does gene Y interact with gene Z?". Null when interaction_type = SUBUNIT.
protein_interaction_uniprot.nb_experiments: Number of IntAct experiments supporting this BINARY interaction (integer; null for SUBUNIT rows). Use as a confidence proxy — higher values indicate better-supported interactions.
protein_interaction_uniprot.description: Free-text description of the interaction. For SUBUNIT rows: full curator prose about complex composition, binding domains, and regulatory context. For BINARY rows: raw CC INTERACTION line. Substring-match on this field when the user asks about a specific complex name, binding partner, or structural context.

species_master_uniprot.taxon_id: NCBI taxonomy identifier as a string (e.g. '9606' for Homo sapiens, '10090' for Mus musculus). Users may ask for 'taxonomy ID', 'taxon ID', or 'NCBI taxon'.
species_master_uniprot.species_code: UniProt species code mnemonic (e.g. 'HUMAN', 'MOUSE', 'RAT', 'AADNV'). Primary key; used in UniProt entry names.
species_master_uniprot.kingdom: Broad taxonomic kingdom code: 'E' for Eukaryota, 'B' for Bacteria, 'V' for Viruses, 'A' for Archaea, 'O' for Other, 'X' for Unclassified. Single-character identifier.
species_master_uniprot.scientific_name: Full Latin binomial scientific name (e.g. 'Homo sapiens', 'Mus musculus', 'Rattus norvegicus'). Users may ask for 'scientific name', 'species', or 'organism'.
species_master_uniprot.common_name: Common colloquial name of the species (e.g. 'Human', 'Mouse', 'Rat'). Users may ask for 'common name' or 'organism'.
species_master_uniprot.synonym: Alternative names for the species. Used to match user queries with non-standard species names.
